full-dataset.t: We start with one collection of **24 labelled examples**. Nothing has been separated yet, so any score measured now would not be a fair test.

shuffle.t: **Shuffle first**, so the split does not depend on the order the data happened to be collected in.

train-split.t: About **70%** go to **TRAIN**. This ratio is an illustration, not a required rule. This is the data the model **learns from**.

validation-split.t: About **15%** go to **VALIDATION**. They are **held out from training** and used to compare choices, such as which model or setting works best.

test-split.t: The rest, about **15%**, go to **TEST**. They stay **locked away until the very end**, so they can give an honest final score.

training.t: Only the **TRAIN** examples fit the model's parameters. The validation and test examples play no part in learning.

validation.t: **VALIDATION** scores compare candidate models and settings. The best one is chosen here, using data the model did not train on.

final-test.t: **TEST** is used **once**, for an unbiased estimate. It was **never used to train or to choose**, which is why its score can be trusted.
